content.text: I’ve completed the brief pass; I’m consolidating Phase 0–1 into implementation-facing requirements and explicit exclusions.

Phase 0–1 requirements matrix from `docs/plan-brief.md`:

| Area | Mandatory for Phase 0–1 | Acceptance / verification | Explicit boundaries |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repository foundation (P0) | Create monorepo structure: `go/{cmd,internal,pkg}`, `python/{src/harness_agents,agents,prompts,tests}`, `proto/harness/{reasoning,workflow,execution,events}/v1`, `schemas`, `migrations`, `deploy`, `docs`, `tests`. | All projects build; tests run through one command; generated files reproducible; CI green. | Separately deployable Go services are architectural skeletons only; business logic remains testable Go packages, not network services. No extra microservices without demonstrated boundary need. |
| Go build system | Go workspace; initial command locations for API, workflow, registry, gateway, execution, verification services; small consumer-owned interfaces and dependency injection. | Build/lint/format/test commands documented and working. | No generic reasoner returning `any`; no workflow/execution methods on reasoning interfaces; generated protobuf code outside domain logic. |
| Python build system | Python project using `uv`; small declarative agent SDK foundation/manifest compiler sufficient for deterministic manifest compilation and validation. | Python manifests validate; equal inputs produce equal bytes/digest. | Python must not mutate workflow state, access DB, run Git/commands, approve, alter scope, lease resources, publish, open PRs, or provide authoritative evidence. Keep it outside production request path. |
| Tooling and CI | Linting, formatting, test commands, Protobuf generation, reproducibility checks, local-development instructions, CI workflow. | One-command test invocation; CI green. | Do not treat generated output as hand-maintained domain code. |
| Protobuf contracts (P1) | Define `reasoning/v1/{common,specification,planning,implementation,review}.proto`; provider-neutral typed contracts. Also establish workflow identifiers, proposal types, and rejection types. | Go contract tests; cross-language serialization/mapping compatibility. | No model provider or live provider routing. |
| Common reasoning request | Include schema version, request/run IDs, optional task ID, stage, attempt, created/expiry timestamps, authority constraints, token/request budgets, input artifact digests, agent-manifest digest. | Contract schema and identity/digest validation tests. | Reject requests/responses violating authority. |
| Authority contract | Exactly proposal-only authority: `mode: proposal_only`; all `may_mutate_kernel_state`, `may_execute_commands`, `may_modify_files`, `may_expand_scope`, `may_approve_work` false. | Authority-violation test path. | Models can propose only; kernel alone authorizes/execut
es/verifies/approves/transitions. |
| Stage proposal shapes | Specification: title/goal/actors/constraints/non-goals/criteria+verification/assumptions/risks/questions. Planning: graph/dependencies/objectives/criterion assignments/path scopes/resources/checks/stops/questions. Implementation: structured changes, expected original digests, criteria map, declared checks, questions/scope-change request. Review: recommendation/findings/severity/category/evidence/actions/unrequested changes/risks. | Types must be defined; full runtime behavior deferred. | Review recommendation is advisory, never approval. |
| Rejection contracts | Stable codes: `SCHEMA_INVALID`, `REQUEST_MISMATCH`, `AUTHORITY_VIOLATION`, `SCOPE_VIOLATION`, `REQUIRED_COVERAGE_MISSING`. Rejection fields: code, summary, details, retryable, request/run/task IDs, attempt, timestamp. | Tests must cover schema, request identity, authority, scope, and coverage paths as contracts where feasible. | First deterministic rejection only; multi-error collection deferred. |
| Validation contract | Preserve validator order: decode/schema → request/attempt identity → artifact/manifest digests → authority → path/resource scope → acceptance coverage → stage policy. No execution side effect before all pass. | Tests assert ordering/no-side-effect principle at contract boundary. | Execution pipeline itself is later. |
| Agent manifest schema | Create `schemas/agent-manifest-v1.schema.json`; require schema version, agent name/version, stage, prompt URI/digest, model capability/parameters, context policy, tool-request policy, output schema, configuration metadata. | Python output validates against schema. | Must forbid credentials/secrets, executable code, shell commands, unrestricted URLs, transitions, approval rules, writable paths, and task-specific scope. |
| Canonical manifest compiler | Validate required fields; reject unsupported stage/direct shell/network/write; sort object keys; normalize values; deterministic canonical JSON; SHA-256 digest; emit manifest + digest. | Identical input has identical canonical artifact and digest. | Task-specific authority comes only from Go kernel. |
| Artifact/digest rules | Canonical artifact digest rules shared across Go and Python; SHA-256 used for manifests/artifacts. | Cross-language contract tests verify canonical JSON and digest parity. | Artifact metadata is a contract now; PostgreSQL/object storage implementation is later. |
| Documentation (required deliverables) | At minimum create/update: `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/resource-analysis.md`, `docs/decision-log.md`, `docs/workflow-state-machine.md`, `docs/reasoning-contracts.md`, `docs/agent-manifest.md`, `docs/development.md`. | Local instructions must identify exact build/test/generation commands. | After each phase update architecture, decision log, resource/security analysis, and test coverage summary. |
| Decision log | Append material decisions using `DEC-XXX` template with decision, options, pros/cons, why, consequences, date. Required initial topics: trusted Go kernel; Python canonical JSON; Protobuf; complete-file replacement first patch format; PostgreSQL metadata; independent verification; no auto merge; fake provider first. | Documentation review. | Record decisions even when implementation is deferred. |
| Resource/security analysis | Document CPU/memory/disk/network/DB/artifact/token/build-test/concurrency expectations; configurable limits for proposal bytes, changed files, file sizes/content, context/output tokens, task/test durations, retries, worktrees, concurrent tasks. | Documentation-level analysis/configuration boundary. | Security posture must preserve no direct model/Python DB access, immutable manifests, deny-default network, no production credentials, no auto merge/deploy. |
| Tests | Unit/contract tests for manifest validation, canonical JSON, SHA-256, proposal identity, rejection types, Protobuf/Go/JSON-schema/Python compatibility. | P0/P1 acceptance above. | Integration/E2E implementation behavior may be scaffolded but full workflows belong to later phases. |

Required architectural facts to encode now:

- Internal service communication is Protobuf/gRPC; Python manifests are canonical JSON.
- PostgreSQL is the planned authority for metadata and object/filesystem storage for large artifacts, but no database runtime/migrations-backed workflow execution is to be implemented in this task.
- Commands are imperative and events are completed facts; defining identifiers/contracts is appropriate, implementing workflow execution is not.
- The full run/task state enumerations and atomic append-only transition rules belong to the Phase 2 kernel state machine, though `docs/workflow-state-machine.md` should document the intended contract.

Prohibited Phase 0–1 scope:

- Workflow execution/state-machine implementation, run/task aggregates, persistence runtime, leases, worktrees, execution/file mutation, verification execution, approvals, PR creation, database runtime, model provider, provider fallback/routing, production credentials, automatic merge/deploy.
- Arbitrary model shell/scripts, unrestricted network, agent-authored policy, autonomous scope expansion, dynamic/self-modifying agents, generalized multi-agent chat, complex UI.
- Any silent requirement expansion; document and stop for extra service/infra dependency/broader access/unapproved migration/production credentials/merge-deploy capability.

Phase-gate reporting requirement: do not claim a phase complete until acceptance passes; final phase report must list changed files, exact commands/results, assumptions, unresolved issues, deviations, and recommended next phase.
